So we need circumference for radius 5: C = 2πr = 10π. Also find circumference of a circle with diameter 10: C = π d = 10π. So both are same. But we should use the provided functions: circle_calculate_area and circle_calculate_circumference. For circumference with diameter, we use circle_calculate_circumference. For area, use circle_calculate_area. For perimeter of circle, maybe use circle_calculate_circumference as well. So we need to call functions twice: one for area, one for circumference. Also circumference for diameter. So two calls: circle_calculate_area with radius 5, circle_calculate_circumference with diameter 10. But we also need circumference for radius 5. We could call circle_calculate_circumference with diameter 10? Wait diameter of radius 5 is 10. So same. So we can just use that. So we need area and perimeter (circumference) for radius 5. And circumference for diameter 10. So we can compute area via circle_calculate_area(5). Perimeter via circle_calculate_circumference(diameter=10). That gives circumference for radius 5. And also circumference for diameter 10 is same. So we can output both.
